notes:
Pass on the fake backend only. The package serves the card's models[0], the MJCF scene musclemimic_models/model/arm/myoarm_bimanual.xml, as a MujocoDriver (device_kind world.sim, mode simulated, risk R0). The step action is the model's data.ctrl; the bridge derives one [-1, 1] bound per actuator from the model's actuator_ctrlrange (126 muscle actuators; the model's default classes state ctrlrange="-1 1" at myoarm_bimanual_assets.xml:37-38, :53-54 and :57-58), and the reset restores the model defaults with mj_resetData. The state is the bridge's time_ms, qpos (76 joints), qvel, ctrl, tick, timestep_ms (0.002 s from myoarm_bimanual_assets.xml:21) and seed. No operator_required limit was needed; no extension id was used, so there is no catalogue_requests entry. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: none; the card's family-config/MujocoDriver shape fits the model. The card lists a second model, musclemimic_models/model/body/myofullbody.xml, which this one-device package does not serve. WHAT IS NOT COVERED: MuJoCo itself is not installed and cannot be installed where the gate runs (no network, no pip). fake.py is a pure Python stand-in for the mujoco library: it parses the MJCF (including its <include> elements) for the 126 actuator control ranges, 76 joints and 0.002 s timestep, but its integration is a placeholder first-order motion; it resolves no muscle, tendon, contact, equality, mesh, texture or sensor model, and no trajectory was compared with MuJoCo. There is no rendering, no hardware and no hardware run. The model and its assets are read from the read-only clone at runtime; the package copies none of them and the clone was not modified. Expected warnings, not failures: G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND (backends["fake"] is the package's stand-in mujoco module object, which the family gate treats as the upstream simulator, so native calls and a fake surface are not recorded), and three G8.NO_UNIT warnings for the bridge-derived simulator inputs seed, ticks and action.ctrl[*]. G4 reported no REF_VALUE warnings. driver.lock.json authored_by is the model id and run id, reviewed_by is null; nothing was human-reviewed or hardware-tested.
